title: They Would Never Forget This Chase.

transcript.text: This is a chase no officer would ever forget. In the evening of February 7, 2024, officers from the Tanti Town Police Department in Arkansas received a distress call from multiple other law enforcement agencies. According to news sources, the police were in pursuit of a stolen U-Haul van, one that allegedly traveled at speeds in excess of 120 miles an hour. Officers didn't know it at the time, but the occupants are in possession of multiple firearms and Molotov cocktails, multiple agencies responded, including the Arkansas State Police, who are known to have a very aggressive pursuit and pit policy. At the vehicle, TVI do not rest the vehicle. What did I just witness? At the initial point of contact for this officer's TIV attempt, commonly referred to as a pit maneuver, the officer's speed tracker indicated he is traveling 101 miles an hour. For comparison, many agencies consider pits above 45 miles per hour to constitute lethal force, as you'll soon discover. Tragically, the officer's push bumper gets hooked on the U-Haul, resulting in complete loss of control of the squad. I'm good. I'm good. I'm good. I'm good. You're all right? I'm good, good. According to news reports, the pursuit began in Locust Grove, Oklahoma, and ended roughly 60 miles away in Springdale, Arkansas. Four patrol vehicles were taken out of commission due to the damages incurred. The suspects allegedly face charges for aggravated assault. assault, criminal conspiracy, possession of destructive devices, fleeing, battery, criminal mischief, and resisting arrest. According to news reports, these suspects are also wanted for attempting to run over police officers located over 700 miles away in Michigan. We found out about this incident thanks to safety vid.org, which caught the crash on this Arkansas DOT camera.
